narrative.overview:
Every answer is treated as an engineering drawing sheet: a white sheet on a pale desk, ruled with hairlines, annotated rather than decorated. Claims in the prose carry item balloons, which are numbered circles, and each balloon points to a row in a parts-list register of sources. A title block under the answer records how it was made. Provenance is the visual subject.

Density is calm and technical. Surfaces are flat, bordered by 1px hairlines, and square-cornered (2-3px). A deep navy rail anchors the left edge. Colour is reserved for state: blue means selection and citation, green means current, red means superseded or conflicting. State is never colour alone.

The system refuses the chat-over-documents default: no message bubbles, no avatars, no gradient send button.
keyCharacteristics: White sheets on a pale grey-green desk, separated by hairlines rather than shadows.
Navy rail with the current page cut out in desk colour.
Item balloons as the single signature mark, matched one-to-one to parts-list rows.
Revision triangles and redline strike-through carry version state.
Barlow for reading, Barlow Semi Condensed for labels and headings, JetBrains Mono for IDs, scores and values.

rules.name: The State-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue, green and red appear only to encode selection, currency, or conflict. Decoration, emphasis and branding stay in navy and neutrals.

rules.name: The Shape-Plus-Colour Rule
rules.body: Every coloured state also changes shape: ok is a filled circle, superseded or failed is a triangle, warning is a small square, unknown is a hollow ring.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Identifiers Rule
rules.body: Anything a person might copy or compare (document ID, score, parameter value) is monospace; prose never is.

rules.name: The Caption-Not-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Uppercase condensed labels are cell captions inside a title block or table head, attached to the value they describe. They are never set above a heading as an introduction.

rules.name: The Hairline-First Rule
rules.body: Separate regions with a 1px rule before reaching for a shadow; shadow is reserved for sheets and dialogs.

dos: Do answer in a sheet: prose with inline balloons, a register of sources, then a title block of cells.
Do match every balloon to a parts-list row, and show superseded versions with the red strike and a red triangle.
Do pair every state colour with a shape or strike (blue selection, green current, red conflict).
Do use hairlines (1px hair or hair-strong) to divide regions; keep radii at 2px (sheets) and 3px (controls).
Do set IDs, scores and values in JetBrains Mono, and let long IDs wrap rather than overflow.
Do keep table overflow inside a scroll wrapper and keep the composer pinned to the thread bottom.
Do honour reduced motion; animations are limited to the live sweep, the row reveal and 120ms state transitions.
donts: Don't use chat bubbles, avatars, or a gradient or glowing send button.
Don't introduce another accent hue; blue, green and red already cover selection, currency and conflict.
Don't use colour alone to signal state.
Don't round surfaces beyond 3px; the balloon is the only circle in the layout.
Don't put uppercase condensed labels above headings as introductions; they are captions inside title-block cells and table heads.
Don't use shadows to separate adjacent regions; use a hairline.
